name: 74MX at the RKC

soil.notes: A rider-oriented roundup calls it classic southwest Florida sugar sand; directories mention sandy sections and a dedicated sand-turn practice track. Older RiderPlanet data lists some loose dirt and some sand.

layout.notes: Described as a legit SX/MX-style layout. Review summaries mention some awkward jump faces/landings and riders wanting bigger jumps on the main track. Mainly suited to beginner and intermediate riders.

conditions.dry: Sugar sand; expect loose, deep sections when dry.
conditions.watering_prep: Reported to be groomed several times a day, notably around midday, and regularly watered.
conditions.seasonal: Fri-Sun 9am-4pm per MX Parks (another aggregator lists extra weekday hours; conflicting). Big bikes ~$40, small bikes ~$20, spectators $10; RV hookups and dry camping. Check Facebook for weather calls. Quads share the property and can chew up bike lines.

rider_reports.says: One rider said not to bother with 74 because it had turned into a quad-focused track; another remembered it as a great track in the past.
Southeast track roundup: classic SW Florida sugar sand, well maintained, a legit SX/MX layout that challenges experienced riders.
Aggregated review summary: good watered soil, multiple tracks for each skill level, some awkward jumps, owners take pride in grooming; complaints about entry price and GPS leading onto back roads.
When it reopened in early 2024, several regulars welcomed it back and one called it the best track he had ridden; a dissenting rider said it had become quad-heavy.

name: Dade City Motocross
address: 36722 State Road 52, Dade City, FL 33525 (behind the Pasco County Fairgrounds)
tracks_on_site: main MX track (lit for night racing)
extended track layout used on select Sunday practices

soil.notes: Several independent sources agree it is a sand/clay mix with sand dominant. Riders and videos describe it as tacky sand; directories list it as mostly sand with clay mixed in. An older (circa 2007) series page described the night track as all clay and the day/extended course as clay with sand sections, so the surface varies by which layout is running. Sand-tire or soft-intermediate tire choice is the common recommendation.

layout.notes: Local press describes a layout with tight turns and many jumps on roughly 100 acres; directories list many small jumps, some larger ones and berms throughout, with no real hills. The Red Bull Day in the Dirt Down South GP course (each March) is a different, mellower wide-open loop through woods, sand and grass plus a paved-road section, built by Dream Traxx; it is not the regular MX layout.

conditions.dry: Rides as tacky sand when moisture is right; expect sand-style ruts to develop as the session wears on. Summer heat on a sandy surface is called out as hard on riders.
conditions.wet: Heavy rain can waterlog the track badly (a 2010 race turned into standing water and first-turn pileups before the crew salvaged it). Plan for afternoon thunderstorm closures in summer.
conditions.late_day: Racing is mainly Saturday night under lights, so the track is raced after a full afternoon of practice and heats; expect it to be rutted and choppier by the late motos. Not directly confirmed by a rider source.
conditions.watering_prep: Listed as groomed and watered, with a starting gate. Track crew reworks it around events.
conditions.seasonal: Year-round schedule: Thursday night practice (50cc early, other classes evening), Saturday morning MX school, Saturday night race series (47th season in 2026, ~36 classes), select Sunday extended-track practices. Hosts Day in the Dirt Down South each March and has hosted Loretta Lynn area qualifiers and Florida Gold Cup rounds.

rider_reports.says: Video uploader describes Dade City as a tacky sand track with lights for night racing, a steady local race series and weekly practice.
Forum poster calls the track great but warns that practice days can be chaotic with traffic.
Family race write-up describes the track as sandy and the August heat as a big factor for young riders.
Race report: heavy rain flooded the track before the motos; riders crashed and got stuck in the first turn while the crew worked to keep it raceable.
Riders at Day in the Dirt Down South described the Dream Traxx-built GP course as fast and flowing.

Reviewer says riding the same prepped dirt as the pros during RCSX week is a unique once-a-year experience, not a practice venue.

name: Gatorback Cycle Park

soil.notes: Old lime-rock quarry site. Riders describe a hard limestone/clay base with sand hauled in over the years, so it rides as a sandy clay rather than a typical deep Florida sand track. Directories variously call it red clay or a hardpack/sand mix; long-time riders consistently say hard limerock-clay base softened by added sand.

layout.notes: Roughly 1.2-mile track with more elevation than most Florida venues, including a drop into the old quarry. Historic big jump known as the Elevator (smaller now than in the 1990s), a triple section, a sandy whoop section in the woods, and a sweeping left near the road that packs hard and slick. Two race tracks can share one start gate.

conditions.dry: Starts tacky and good in the morning when the clay is fresh; as the sun bakes it, it goes hard and slick on the packed sections while the sandy parts break into ruts and bumps.
conditions.wet: Heavy rain has flooded the pits and track during Mini O's week and cancelled racing; after drying, riders reported soft but well-formed ruts. Mud adds deep ruts.
conditions.late_day: Gets very rough in the afternoon; deep ruts and large braking bumps by end of day at big events (photos from 2023 Mini O's showed waist-deep ruts on kids' bikes).
conditions.watering_prep: Prepped and tilled for organized race weekends; sand has been added over time to soften the hard base. No regular open practice, so prep is event-driven.
conditions.seasonal: Main use is winter and Thanksgiving-week events (Florida Winter AM series, Thor Mini O's in late November) plus the Southeast Youth Regional in early June.

rider_reports.says: Several long-time riders agree the base is hard limestone/clay from the old quarry with sand mixed in over the years; one compares the current surface to Budds Creek and says it gets very rough and rutted, another says it is best in the first motos while the clay is fresh and brutal by afternoon.
Riders said Gatorback's dirt was once nearly the same hard clay-limerock mix as Hardrock, but has had a lot of sand mixed in recent years.
Youth regional organizer notes describe the track as softer than it used to be with deep ruts because sand has been worked into the harder dirt.
A racer at Mini O's said that after flooding rain earlier in the week, the track came back better than expected with soft, good ruts and credited the track crew.
Mini O's recap noted mud, very deep ruts and braking bumps bigger than speed bumps, calling the track gnarly late in the week.

conditions.watering_prep: Deep-tilled for races (described as shaped like a national). Prepped and watered on its limited riding days.
conditions.seasonal: Summer heat and humidity are severe; hosted the 2017 MXGP of USA and Pro Motocross nationals 2019-2020. Closed to normal open practice; riding by posted days, training groups or races.

rider_reports.says: Race breakdown described a sand-dominant track with clay veins and clay on jump faces, abrupt transitions from deep sand to hard base on corner exits that made the rear tire spin up, and a track that got very rough and wore riders down by the second moto.
A former Florida pro previewing the national called it typical Florida: flat, sandy and rough, with limited man-made elevation and heat as the main challenge.
Amateur race report said the crew tilled the pro track for amateurs and it got as rough as a national; younger riders found it rougher than their usual tracks.
A pro quoted in the MXGP announcement called it a classic Florida sand track with clay jumps and dark sand straights that starts fast and gets rough.
Local riders note it is the biggest track near Jacksonville but closed to open practice; check the website for riding days.
